title: North Providence planning board reviews draft tree ordinance update
text:
← Back to the wire

North Providence planning board reviews draft tree ordinance update
Tree Warden Tim Thorp told the board the new ordinance would create a voluntary significant inherited tree registry funded by a dedicated tree preservation fund rather than tax dollars.
The North Providence Planning Board on Wednesday reviewed a draft update to the town's tree ordinance that includes a proposed voluntary significant inherited tree registry, discussed during a meeting at North Providence Council Chambers, 2000 Smith Street.
THE PROPOSAL Tim Thorp, Tree Warden for North Providence, presented the draft, which includes a tree preservation fund alongside the registry. "The idea would be that there is a fund dedicated to tree preservation in the town," Thorp said, adding that it would not be funded by taxes but that people could donate to it and that fines would go into it.
Thorp said the fund would not be zeroed out annually and "could help residents with private tree matters that they could apply for that money." He said he hoped it would "acrue to a matter where it would be helpful to people who have significant trees," and that the registry beneath it would enable people to make applications to use those funds.
ORIGIN OF THE IDEA Asked whether the registry concept came from the Green Infrastructure Center, Thorp said, "No, I came up with that one myself. They liked it." He compared the structure to an existing mechanism in the town: "We have something set up like this for the land trust where a percentage of each building permit gets put into a trust fund."
NEXT STEPS Board chairman noted the ordinance change would need to be ratified by the town council. Thorp agreed, saying, "It would. Yeah, that that's how it's proposed to us." The board asked Thorp to provide a document identifying all specific changes from the 1995 ordinance, which he agreed to deliver to Town Planner Brent before the board's next meeting, newly scheduled for Nov. 10.
